title: Dairy Quality Control, Chemical Quality Assurance, Packaging, Hygiene and Adulteration Detection
shortDescription: Quality systems for dairy: tests, contaminants, packaging technologies and plant hygiene including CIP.
genZNote: Dairy QC is where 'looks fine' gets audited by a lab. CIP = clean without disassembling, alkali first and acid after.

sections.heading: Quality Control and Chemical Quality Assurance
bullets: Platform tests: temperature, odour, COB, alcohol test, acidity, fat/SNF (milk analysers), density, adulterant spot tests, antibiotics.
Laboratory microbiology: SPC, coliforms, thermodurics, yeast and mould, pathogens by PCR; process checks: phosphatase, peroxidase, turbidity (sterilised milk).

Chemical quality assurance: antibiotic residues (β-lactam tests), pesticide and heavy-metal residues, aflatoxin M1 (FSSAI limit 0.5 µg/kg milk), melamine, adulterants; sensory evaluation by scorecards; HACCP and ISO 22000/9001 for plants.
Adulteration detection: see Milk Adulterants lesson; confirm with FTIR/ultrasonic analysers and reference methods; legal samples are tested at notified labs.

sections.heading: Dairy Packaging Technologies
bullets: Pasteurised milk: polyethylene (LDPE/LLDPE) pouches, PET/HDPE bottles; UHT: aseptic multilayer cartons (paperboard, PE, aluminium foil) with sterile filling; glass bottles for premium milk; tubs and cups for dahi; foil/laminates for ghee, butter, paneer; vacuum packs and MAP for cheese.
Light protection: riboflavin sensitises photo-oxidation, giving off-flavours — use opaque packs.
Requirements: food-grade materials, complete labelling, cold chain for pasteurised products.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Dairy quality assurance combines raw-milk testing, process verification, residue control, protective packaging and rigorous plant hygiene such as CIP.
keyFacts: Aflatoxin M1 limit in milk: 0.5 µg/kg.
Phosphatase and peroxidase tests are process checks.

commonTraps: Do not mix aflatoxin B1 (feed) with M1 (milk).
mustRemember: CIP: alkali for organic soil; acid for minerals.

sources.name: De Sa: Dairy Science and Technology
